title: Muse Code: Meta's New Terminal Coding Agent, Explained

facts.fact: Meta released Muse Code in beta on August 5, 2026, as a terminal-based coding agent.
facts.quote: released in beta on _August 5, 2026_

facts.fact: Muse Code installs with a single command on macOS or Linux.
facts.quote: It installs with a single command on macOS or Linux

facts.fact: Muse Code's Standard tier is listed at $1.25 per 1M input tokens.
facts.quote: Standard Tier ($1.25/$4.25 per M tokens): Keeps your data private.

facts.fact: Muse Code's Standard tier is listed at $4.25 per 1M output tokens.
facts.quote: Standard Tier ($1.25/$4.25 per M tokens): Keeps your data private.

facts.fact: Muse Code's Standard tier is listed at $0.15 per 1M cached input tokens.
facts.quote: | **Standard** | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 | Meta does **not** train on your prompts or completions |

facts.fact: Meta states that the Standard tier does not train on users' prompts or completions.
facts.quote: Meta does **not** train on your prompts or completions

facts.fact: Muse Code's Contributor tier is listed at $0.10 per 1M input tokens.
facts.quote: Contributor Tier ($0.10/$0.20 per M tokens): Up to 21x cheaper, but Meta trains future models on your prompts and code.

facts.fact: Muse Code's Contributor tier is listed at $0.20 per 1M output tokens.
facts.quote: Contributor Tier ($0.10/$0.20 per M tokens): Up to 21x cheaper, but Meta trains future models on your prompts and code.

facts.fact: Muse Code's Contributor tier is listed at $0.002 per 1M cached input tokens.
Under the Contributor tier, Meta trains its models on users' prompts and completions.
facts.quote: Meta **trains its models** on your prompts and completions; capped at 60 requests per minute

facts.fact: The Muse Code Contributor tier is capped at 60 requests per minute.
facts.quote: capped at 60 requests per minute

facts.fact: The page states that the Contributor tier is roughly 12.5x cheaper than Standard on input tokens.
facts.quote: The Contributor tier is roughly 12.5x cheaper on input and 21x cheaper on output than Standard

facts.fact: Meta reports that Muse Spark 1.2 scores 82.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 on its own evaluation harness.
facts.quote: scoring **82.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1**

facts.fact: Meta reports that Muse Spark 1.2 scores 59.3% on DeepSWE 1.1 on its own evaluation harness.
facts.quote: **59.3% on DeepSWE 1.1**

facts.fact: Meta reported a Terminal-Bench 2.1 score of 80.0 for its predecessor Muse Spark 1.1.
facts.quote: On the **predecessor model, Muse Spark 1.1**, Meta reported a Terminal-Bench 2.1 score of 80.0.

facts.fact: Vals AI's independent testing measured Muse Spark 1.1 at 69.29 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (third-party result).
facts.quote: Vals AI's independent testing measured 69.29

facts.fact: The Terminal-Bench team's official verified leaderboard lists Muse Spark 1.1 at 76.2% (third-party result).
facts.quote: the Terminal-Bench team's own official verified leaderboard entry for Muse Spark 1.1 came in at 76.2%

facts.fact: Artificial Analysis independently evaluated Muse Spark 1.2 at around 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, versus Meta's claimed 82.9% (third-party estimate).
facts.quote: independent evaluation from Artificial Analysis puts it around 80% against Meta's claimed 82.9%

facts.fact: Vals AI's common-harness leaderboard ranks Muse Spark 1.2 14th (third-party ranking).
facts.quote: Vals AI's common-harness leaderboard, by contrast, ranks it **14th**.

facts.fact: The highest independently verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 score reported on the page is 83.8%, posted by Claude Fable 5 running in Claude Code (third-party).
facts.quote: the highest independently verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 score posted by any model so far belongs to Claude Fable 5 running in Claude Code, at 83.8%
